anti_generic_signature_read: Asked what was specific rather than generic: 'The terrain tiles are the memorable part -- the incised sunburst rosettes, the dense field of little pyramids, and the sunken black square fenced with spikes are specific and not something a generic checkers set would have. The ring planet's ring being a real separate disc passing through the sphere is also specific.' And, on the world this revision corrects, the cue that decides it, drawn by the critic unprompted in image 9: the cyan ball 'does have a continuous band over its pole and I called it "a real beach-ball stripe" -- so I demonstrably could still see a closed band when one was present, and there isn't one on Neptune.'
blind_action_read: 'Two players place and move planet pieces across grid squares, past or into hazard terrain; the trays hold the pieces off-board. Nothing in the images shows a mechanism -- nothing hinges, slides, spins or latches. The rings, spikes and cones are all static geometry.' That last sentence is the correct read of this product: nothing in the set moves against anything else, and motion is recorded as unverified rather than passed.
blind_form_read: 'Flat: the board slab, a plain thick rectangular plate, and the two trays. Cut in: the cell divisions are shallow recessed grooves; the trays' pockets are scalloped dish depressions; one cell is a black square sunk below the board; the cyan and orange tiles carry engraved starburst/rosette line art that is incised, not raised. Standing proud: the pieces -- a cylindrical puck (some white, some black), a short narrower cylindrical neck, then a full sphere sitting on that neck ... fields of tiny pyramid bumps fill several tan cells; slender cones stand on the cyan tiles, the orange tiles and around the black sunken square ... one ball carries a thin flat disc ring cutting through it at an angle. Each puck rim has a tiny raised pixel-font glyph.'
blind_held_read: Critic B, unprompted, before anything was revealed: 'A board game. Image 1 shows a flat rectangular grey playing slab ruled into a grid of square cells, populated with roughly twenty ball-on-a-puck playing pieces, plus two separate flat grey trays off to the side whose rows of scalloped oval pockets are obviously piece storage. Handed one piece on its own I'd say "a small planet marble glued to a checker/draughts puck". Handed the whole thing I'd say "a solar-system chess/checkers set".'
blind_relationship_read: 'Ball sits on neck sits on puck; puck sits within one grid cell. Pucks are sized to the cell ... The trays are wholly separate, not docked to the board, and their pockets are round dishes that would cradle a puck or a ball but don't lock either. Nothing causes anything: it's an arrangement, not a machine.'
blind_subjects_read: Named unprompted: 'Planets. I can name a banded cream-and-orange giant with a red oval spot; a pale yellow one with a flat ring; a small red mottled one; a small blue-and-green marbled one; a bright cyan one with a white band; a deep navy one with white slashes; a small grey-white one with a crater dimple. The terrain tiles read as an asteroid or rubble field (pyramid bumps), sun or star tiles (engraved radiating rosettes with cones), and a black pit with spikes around it that reads as a hazard or black hole. Two piece colours, white pucks and black pucks, so two sides.'

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B, asked blind and answering for each piece: 'No -- for both pieces.' It stated the test itself before applying it: a true encircling belt seen down the axis 'would appear as a closed concentric ring -- an unbroken annulus all the way round the disc', and instead image 7 shows arcs 'with more than half the circumference empty' and image 8 arcs 'at the top-left and right with clear gaps'. Both opposite-side views are bare. Unprompted, it drew the contrast that proves it could still see a closed band: the cyan world beside it 'does have a continuous band over its pole', which it called 'a real beach-ball stripe' -- 'but it is the other ball, not this one.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The white markings must be SHORT ARCS, not closed bands: no streak circles the planet.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind: 'a scatter of narrow, pointed, lens- or almond-shaped strokes'. It could not count them from renders and said so, raising 'possibly more than eight streaks' and 'possible longitude bunching' as checks against the model rather than findings. Both are answered on the model: `parts/neptune_atlas.STREAKS` carries exactly eight, at eight different latitudes from -52 to +47, eight different longitudes spanning 133 degrees, and eight different lengths from 46 to 90 degrees of longitude, no two equal. `measure/neptune-atlas-resolution.md` tabulates all eight; the ninth white body is the spot's companion.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Six to eight streaks, of different lengths, at different latitudes, at different longitudes so they do not stack into a column.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind, without being told either clause: the strokes are 'each tapering to a sharp tip at both ends', and 'like brush flicks or claw marks' -- which is a description of varied angles, not of a level set. The source carries tilts of 3 to 12 degrees with alternating signs and a rounded half-disc at each tapered end.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A slight tilt of a few degrees off the parallel on most of them, and a rounded or tapered end rather than a square cut.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind described both spot frames as busy -- image 3 'busy with slashes', image 4 likewise -- and could not count the ratio from renders, saying so. The ratio is measured in `measure/neptune-facing.md`: 6 of 8 at the hero frame and 6 of 8 at the state sheet on the Sol piece, 8 of 8 at both on the Anti-Sol piece, against a facing floor of +0.30.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A clear majority of the streaks must face the camera at both product frames on both pieces.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind: 'a squat grey-charcoal oval low on the face', and on comparison it confirmed the union is gone -- 'I saw no two-lobe pinch or waist, which is what a circle union would show'. It also read straight segments on the outline; that is disproved in `measure/neptune-flush.md`, which measures the ring's worst departure from the true ellipse at 0.0305 mm, 8 per cent of one nozzle, on a marking 5.35 mm across, and shows the same frame magnified four times as a continuous smooth ellipse whose only stepping is the single-pixel staircase `render_review` puts on every boundary in the image.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The dark spot becomes ONE OVAL about twice as wide as it is tall, centred at latitude -22, still dark_gray -- replacing the two-circle union.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind: 'Immediately beside it sits a small pale lozenge', and on comparison 'it exists, it is smaller, and it sits toward the equator-facing edge ... up is equator-ward for a southern spot', and on the Sol piece 'it is at least clearly detached'. The gap is 0.61 mm, measured on the two exact rings in `measure/neptune-atlas-resolution.md` -- a nozzle and a half. Every stated clause is met. What the critic judged NOT met is the sentence explaining why the correction wants it: it read the companion as 'a stray fragment' rather than as the bright cloud belonging to the spot. That shortfall is recorded in `largest_risk` and in the product limitations rather than being written off here.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The spot gains a small bright WHITE companion cloud just off its equator-facing edge, clearly smaller than the spot, clearly separate from it, with the gap wider than the 0.4 mm nozzle.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind asserted the opposite -- the markings 'are solid raised lenses that break the ball's silhouette' with 'thin overhanging slivers'. `measure/neptune-flush.md` measures every point of every marking body on both armies at 10.945000 mm from the globe centre against a globe radius of 10.945000 mm: exact tangency, nothing proud to a millionth of a millimetre, because `parts/world.py` SPLITS the ball rather than adding to it. Shown that measurement, the critic withdrew both verdicts in writing -- 'I asserted geometry from a silhouette, and a measurement of the actual solids beats that' -- and identified the cause itself as a coincident-surface artefact of a renderer that does not antialias.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: nothing protrudes, and no downward-facing surface was added.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B could not judge this from images and said so: 'I have no before-state to compare against.' It is answered deterministically instead. `measure/revision-part-hashes.md`: 20 of the 24 printed geometries are byte-identical to the published set, the other four differ only in an exporter occurrence counter diffed line by line in this run, and both Neptune parts are byte-identical too. `measure/occurrence-geometry.md`: of 212 occurrence labels, everything outside `neptune_sol_*` and `neptune_anti_*` is identical in solid count, exact volume and bounding box.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: nothing else in the rest of the set changed.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind read them as 'the same object, not mirrored', reasoning from the marking handedness; shown the set's own definition it withdrew the inference -- 'mirroring is the obliquity sign plus a reversed disc draft, which is a tilt reversal, not a chirality flip of the marking pattern -- so same handedness is exactly what that definition predicts' -- and called its observations consistent with the requirement. `measure/neptune-mirror.md` measures it: the same roles, filaments and solid counts on both armies, the dark spot and seven of the nine white bodies identical in volume to 0.0001 mm3, and the two that differ named with their cause -- the disc's own cut, which is not mirrored with the lean, clipping the two deepest southern streaks on the Sol piece.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: the two pieces are still mirrors in the way this set defines one.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Critic B blind: 'I reported exactly one dark oval per face, no second spot. No polar brightening: in the polar views I described discrete crescent arcs with gaps, not a brightened cap. No ring arcs on this ball -- the ring I noted in image 1 was on the pale-yellow ringed world, a different piece. No fourth colour: I saw blue, white and grey.' The globe carries `blue`, `white` and `dark_gray` and nothing else.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: nothing else added -- no second dark spot, no polar brightening, no ring arcs, no fourth filament.

largest_risk: The critic's, in its own words and not softened. Asked the diagnostic question cold -- does the pale mark beside the dark spot read as a second, brighter cloud belonging to it, or as a stray fragment -- critic B answered: 'It does not read as a companion bright cloud belonging to the spot; it reads as a stray fragment, a detached chip of the same slash material that happened to land nearby.' Critic A said the same thing of two earlier and quite different versions of it. Every stated clause of that requirement is met and measured -- white, north of the spot, half its length, 0.61 mm clear of it, a nozzle and a half -- but the sentence explaining why the correction wants it, that it is what stops the spot reading as a smudge, is not achieved in an independent reader's eye. Three repairs were spent on it (a compact oval, then a long wisp, then a crescent drawn parallel to the spot's own rim at constant clearance) and none of them moved the reading. WHAT I WOULD CHANGE, which is the sentence the owner acts on: the obstacle is contrast, not placement. `dark_gray` #6F6E6D on `blue` #004EA8 separates 42 of 255 luma levels, so the spot itself reads as a grey smudge -- critic B's word -- and a white mark beside a smudge has nothing to belong to. The correction fixes the spot's filament as `dark_gray`, so this run could not test the alternative. Give Neptune `black` for the spot, or a darker globe, and the companion has an object to be the bright edge of. Second, smaller risk, and the same root: critic B's one-line verdict on the streaks was 'Paint -- I'd hand it over saying the white marks look like slashes of paint or stuck-on decals, not weather.' That is the owner's own 1.5 mm width decision working exactly as written -- six to twelve times the reference cloud width, chosen for legibility at the set's viewing scale -- combined with a flush inlay's hard edge, which no world in this set can soften. It is reported, not repaired.
resolution: Four review rounds, three focused repairs, two critics; geometry frozen as reviewed, no source changed after round 4 except documentation. Round 1 failed on the correction's own test -- 'painted stripes' in the blind text. Repair 1 skewed the taper, bowed each centreline, widened the tilts to 3-12 degrees and re-solved all eight longitudes against the four cameras at once; round 2 read them as 'curved tapered sweeps' and 'stripe' and 'beach ball' never returned. Repair 2 took the spot's ring from 22 to 40 vertices and the streak sampling to 0.60 mm. Repair 3 redrew the companion as a crescent parallel to the spot's rim. THREE OF CRITIC B'S FOUR BLOCKING FINDINGS WERE DISPROVED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT, and the fourth is carried in largest_risk rather than dismissed: 'the markings are solid raised lenses that break the silhouette' -- every marking point measures at exactly the globe radius, nothing proud to 1e-6 mm, and the critic withdrew it in writing; 'the spot is a coarse low-segment polygon' -- worst chord error 0.0305 mm, 8 per cent of a nozzle; 'possibly more than eight streaks' and 'possible longitude bunching' -- exactly eight, at eight distinct longitudes spanning 133 degrees. One finding is a requirement conflict, not a defect, in the critic's own framing: the bare far hemisphere is 'the arithmetic consequence of requirement 2'. Print status is sealed digitally-verified-not-print-ready with print_ready_claim false and an empty gate map; motion is unverified, never passed. measure/signature-review-protocol.md and measure/neptune-flush.md carry the detail.
reviewer: Two independent native critics, four rounds, neither shown the Wish, the concept or any file but the nine images; the last round was unprimed. measure/signature-review-protocol.md is the full account.
